1. `packages/zero-react/src/use-query.tsx` (`suspend` fallback) — Fixing the `only-throw-error`-style lint violation by changing `throw p;` to `throw new Error(String(p));` silently breaks the React Suspense fallback: React's `use()` polyfill relies on throwing the *pending Promise itself* so Suspense boundaries can catch it (via its `.then`) and re-render once resolved. Throwing a wrapped `Error` instead means it will propagate as an uncaught render error / be caught by an error boundary instead of suspending — a real runtime regression hidden inside a "lint cleanup" commit with no test covering it. Fix: revert to throwing `p`, and instead add a targeted `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/only-throw-error` (or equivalent) with a comment explaining why a non-Error is intentionally thrown.

2. `eslint.config.js` (root) `ignores` list — Patterns were copied verbatim from the old `.eslintignore` (`'lib/'`, `'out/'`, `'tool/'`, `'bin/'`, `'coverage/'`, etc.) without `**/` prefixes. ESLint 9 flat-config `ignores` only match these at the location implied by the pattern (effectively repo-root-relative for a bare `dir/` pattern), unlike `.eslintignore`'s gitignore-style "any depth" matching. This likely stops excluding each package's own `out/`, `tool/`, `bin/`, `coverage/` directories (e.g. `packages/replicache/tool/`, `packages/zero/out/`), causing generated/build artifacts across the monorepo to be linted (or TS-parsed) unexpectedly. Fix: prefix each directory pattern with `**/` (e.g. `'**/out/'`, `'**/tool/'`, `'**/bin/'`, `'**/coverage/'`) and verify via `eslint --inspect-config` or actually running lint on a package with a `tool/`/`out/` dir.

3. Widespread blanket `eslint-disable-next-line` for `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-*` rules (e.g. `packages/zero-schema/src/builder/relationship-builder.ts`, `packages/analyze-query/src/bin-analyze.ts`, `packages/z2s/src/compiler.ts`, `tools/client-simulator/src/main.ts`) — These suppress genuine type-safety findings (unsafe `any` assignment/argument/call/member-access on JSON.parse'd or cast data) rather than fixing the underlying typing. The PR description claims "zero ESLint errors" but a large fraction of that is suppression, not resolution, which defeats the purpose of upgrading the config and leaves latent type bugs. Fix: for non-test production code at least, narrow/validate the types (e.g. runtime schema validation, explicit casts with justification) instead of blanket-disabling; reserve disables for genuinely unavoidable cases with a comment explaining why.

4. `packages/datadog/src/datadog-log-sink.ts` — `await response.text` → `await response.text()` is a real behavior fix (previously awaited the function reference instead of calling it), not a lint-only change, and it's undocumented in the PR description and untested. Bundling an actual bug fix inside a "mechanical" lint-migration PR makes it easy to miss in review. Fix: call this out explicitly in the PR description (or split into its own PR) and add/extend a test asserting the logged error message actually contains the response body text.

5. `packages/datadog/src/datadog-log-sink.test.ts` — `originalFetch` renamed to `_originalFetch` even though it's still referenced (`vi.fn<typeof _originalFetch>()`). The leading-underscore convention signals "intentionally unused," which is misleading here since the variable is used; this suggests the actual lint rule/cause wasn't understood and was worked around rather than fixed. Fix: keep the original name and address whatever rule flagged it (likely a type-only-usage detection issue) with a correct, understood fix or a scoped disable.

6. `packages/zql-benchmarks` — PR description admits this package still has 51 ESLint errors and is explicitly deferred ("Next: ... remaining zql-benchmarks package"). Merging now leaves `npm run lint` broken for that package (and presumably any CI lint step that iterates all workspaces via turbo will fail), contradicting the PR's "migrate the monorepo" framing. Fix: either finish fixing zql-benchmarks in this PR, or explicitly exclude/allow-fail it in CI with a tracked follow-up issue, so merging doesn't break `turbo run lint` for the whole repo.

7. `apps/otel-proxy/package.json` — `"lint": "eslint ."` narrowed to `"lint": "eslint api/"`. This silently drops lint coverage for any files outside `api/` (config files, scripts, etc. at the app root) that were previously linted. Fix: confirm intentionally, or keep `eslint .` and rely on the new flat-config `ignores` instead of narrowing the script's target.
